question: Who among the following rulers was a part of the Tripartite Struggle for the possession of Kannauj?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dharmapala**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dharmapala** was one of the significant rulers involved in the Tripartite Struggle for the possession of Kannauj.
 
• The Tripartite Struggle was a prolonged conflict among three powerful dynasties: the **Gurjara-Pratiharas**, the **Palas**, and the **Rashtrakutas**.
 
• Dharmapala was the ruler of the **Pala Dynasty** and played a crucial role in the contest for Kannauj, a region of strategic importance in Northern India.
 
• During his reign, Dharmapala extended his influence over Northern India and sought to establish his supremacy over Kannauj.
 
• The struggle for Kannauj had significant implications for the control of trade routes and political dominance in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Tripartite Struggle** lasted for nearly two centuries and was characterized by shifting alliances and frequent battles.
 
• The city of **Kannauj** was highly coveted due to its prime location and economic significance.
 
• Other notable rulers involved in the Tripartite Struggle include **Rashtrakuta King Dhruva** and **Gurjara-Pratihara King Nagabhata II**.
 
• The struggle eventually weakened all three dynasties, paving the way for the rise of new powers in the Indian subcontinent.
